ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory: screen all proposed directors, officers, beneficial owners, and authorized signatories against FINTRAC-defined foreign politically exposed persons under PCMLTFA ss. 9.1-9.3; United Nations Security Council sanctions implemented under the United Nations Act; Canadian autonomous sanctions under the Special Economic Measures Act and associated regulations (including Russia, Belarus, Iran, Syria, Venezuela, and Myanmar listings); and OFAC/OFAC-SDN screening as a contractual condition of USD-denominated Apple App Store and Google Play payout rails. Enhanced due diligence applies to FATF high-risk jurisdictions, with adverse-media monitoring and annual re-screening embedded in the corporate compliance calendar.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_license_trigger_assessment: ISIC 5820 online game publishing does not require a federal or provincial gaming licence; as long as in-app purchases settle through Apple and Google as merchant-of-record, the Mexican? No — the entity is not a money services business under PCMLTFA s. 5(h); if transferable or off-platform-convertible in-game tokens are introduced, MSB characterization must be re-assessed prior to launch.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Corporations Canada Online Filing Centre (corporationscanada.ic.gc.ca) and the National Nuans Name Search portal (nuans.com)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: CBCA s. 10 and the Canada Business Corporations Regulations, 2001 require a name composed of a distinctive element and a descriptive element, or a numeric name. Names may be filed in English, French, or bilingual form and must be distinguishable from existing federal, provincial, and territorial names and registered trademarks. Non-Latin scripts (Cyrillic, CJK, Arabic, etc.) are not accepted as the statutory corporate name; a Latin-alphabet or French-character transliteration is required, while the original-script brand may be protected concurrently under trademarks at CIPO in a non-Western script mark.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: No statutory extension of the 90-day NUANS validity window exists; a fresh NUANS report is required after expiry. On rejection, the applicant should: (1) obtain the Director's written refusal notice; (2) within 30 days submit a written reconsideration request to the Director, Corporations Canada, attaching a fresh NUANS report, submission evidence, and legal argument distinguishing the conflicting name; (3) file a parallel alternative name reservation as a fallback; (4) if the reconsideration is unsuccessful, seek judicial review before the Federal Court under s. 18.1 of the Federal Courts Act, RSC 1985, c F-7, within 30 days of the final refusal; and (5) refrain from trading under the contested name pending resolution to avoid CBCA s. 12 exposure and passing-off liability.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted: CBCA s. 19 requires only a registered office in Canada with a specified street address (not a post-office box) open during business hours for service of process; a licensed corporate-service-provider virtual office satisfies this requirement and is accepted practice for a digital-only MMORPG publisher under ISIC 5820. No physical premises, retail presence, or data-residency condition attaches to the publishing activity.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low (~5% annualized): FINTRAC and the CRA normally conduct document-based and desk reviews for non-regulated digital publishers; unannounced physical inspections are reserved for money services businesses, banks, and financial intermediaries. Inspection risk would only materialize if the in-app-purchase structure were recharacterized as virtual-currency dealing under PCMLTFA s. 5(h), which is mitigated by routing all payments through Apple and Google merchant payout rails.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Canada Business Corporations Act (CBCA), R.S.C. 1985, c. C-44, ss. 5, 6, 8, 19, 101, 106, 126 and related regulations; Articles of Incorporation submitted under Form 2 (CBCA).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Corporations Canada, Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada (ISED)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital is prescribed under the CBCA; shares may be issued without par value. The corporation must maintain a registered office in Canada and satisfy Canadian director residency requirements. No statutory escrow account is required for share subscriptions; consideration may be paid in money, property, or past services at fair value.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: BE IT RESOLVED THAT, at the first meeting of the board of directors of the Corporation: (1) the subscription for 100 common shares by the sole incorporator is accepted, and a share certificate shall be issued upon full payment; (2) the registered office is adopted at [street address, city, province] as the registered office, and the Secretary is directed to file the prescribed notice with Corporations Canada; (3) [Name] is appointed President, [Name] Secretary, and [Name] Treasurer, with authority and duties established in the by-laws; and (4) the officers are authorized to open bank accounts, execute agreements, and take all steps necessary to give effect to these resolutions.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporations Canada, Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada (ISED); NUANS search by registered provider.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Perform a NUANS search for the proposed corporate name through an approved service provider or Corporations Canada. If the name is available, file a Name Reservation Request to reserve the name for 90 days; alternatively, elect to incorporate as a numbered company to avoid a name dispute.
required_dossiers: Instruction Letter or Signed Name Search Request
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is refused, adopt a revised name or use the corporate number; the company may later apply for a distinctive name change after incorporation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporations Canada (online filing services) / legal counsel.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft and execute Form 2, Articles of Incorporation, specifying the required particulars, including corporate name, province of registered office, classes and any special rights of shares, restrictions on share transfer, and the minimum/maximum number of directors. Ensure at least one director is a resident Canadian within the meaning of the CBCA, unless a permitted exception applies. Include director consents in the filing package.
required_dossiers: Consent to Act as Director (CBCA form)
NUANS Report (if using a distinctive name)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Articles are incomplete or non-compliant, correct the errors and refile; a corporation may proceed by numbered name if time does not permit name clearance.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of Incorporation Application and Payment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporations Canada Online Filing Centre or mail/courier to Corporations Canada, Ottawa.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Transmit the completed Articles with the requisite statutory filing fee using Corporations Canada's secure online portal (credit card) or by courier (certified cheque). The filing will be processed on a first-in, first-out basis and the Certificate of Incorporation will be issued electronically. Upon approval, obtain the incorporation certificate and corporate number.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a query is raised, the applicant has 60 days to respond; otherwise the application lapses. Re-filing after correction is possible; the filing fee is generally not refundable.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Board Resolution and Organizational Filings
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Directors and corporate secretary (internal corporate records).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting or obtain unanimous written consent. Pass the first board resolution approving the share subscription, registered office, officers, and banking. Issue share certificates, open the corporate minute book, adopt the by-laws, and complete a corporate file. File Form 20 (Notice of Registered Office and Directors) with Corporations Canada within 15 days of incorporation.
required_dossiers: Corporate Minute Book and Share Registers
Form 20 – Notice of Registered Office and Directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If Form 20 is filed late, file it immediately; Corporations Canada may issue a compliance notice. Ratification by subsequent board resolution can cure procedural omissions.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: CRA Business Number and Tax Account Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) – Business Registration Online (BRO) or telephone registration.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Using the Certificate of Incorporation and the directors' information, register with the CRA for a Business Number, and open programme accounts for corporate income tax, GST/HST, and payroll (if the first hire is imminent). Provide NAICS/ISIC code 511210/5820 and the corporate mailing address. Register for any provincial tax accounts where revenue is generated, if applicable.
required_dossiers: CRA RC1 Application or Online Registration Data
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the CRA registration is rejected or questioned, contact the CRA business registry to verify details and re-submit; corrections may be made via CRA My Business Account.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Municipal Building and Licensing Department (city-specific) and provincial occupational health and safety regulator (e.g., provincial Ministry of Labour); no federal industrial licensing board has jurisdiction over ISIC 5820 software publishing.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: General Business / Occupancy Permit (if the corporation leases office premises) / Fire Safety Occupancy Certificate (where required by municipal fire code)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environment and Climate Change Canada (ECCC) and provincial environmental ministry with jurisdiction (e.g., Ontario Ministry of the Environment, Conservation and Parks).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: No EIA required for pure software publishing; classified as 'Non-prescribed, exempt' under the federal Impact Assessment Act if no physical facility is constructed. Only municipal/provincial waste and e-waste rules apply to office operations.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No wastewater or VOC process emissions generated. If backup generators or battery storage are present, applicable thresholds under the Canadian Environmental Protection Act, 1999 (CEPA) and local sewer by-laws apply; e-waste must be managed under provincial electronics waste diversion programmes.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire marshal inspection and fire safety plan approval; occupancy permit/certificate of compliance under the provincial fire code; compliance with occupational health and safety legislation for computer workstation ergonomics and electrical safety; registration for workers' compensation with the applicable provincial board.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency / Agence du revenu du Canada; CRA My Business Account portal via https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency.html
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity must obtain a federal Business Number (BN) by submitting Form RC1 (or using CRA's online Business Registration service) and requesting the appropriate program accounts, including a GST/HST program account when the entity makes taxable supplies in Canada. CRA validates the legal identity, ownership, representative authority, and jurisdictional information, then issues the BN which serves as the statutory tax identifier for income tax, GST/HST, payroll, and other federal programs. The BN is generally issued within 5-10 business days and no minimum capital is required; a non-resident corporation may also incorporate under the Canada Business Corporations Act or register extra-provincially where required.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation; Canadian-resident corporations are taxed on worldwide income, while non-resident corporations are taxed on Canadian-source business income attributable to a permanent establishment and on certain Canadian-source passive income through Part XIII withholding or Part XIV branch tax; no pass-through taxation is available.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada does not operate a U.S.-style check-the-box regime; classification follows the legal form under the Canada Business Corporations Act. Relevant statutory elections include the s.216 Income Tax Act election for non-residents to report Canadian rental or timber income on a net basis instead of gross Part XIII withholding, the s.217 election for certain employment income, and various anti-hybrid/FAPI anti-deferral rules that do not permit elective entity classification.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (Goods and Services Tax / Harmonised Sales Tax); federal GST of 5% is imposed under the Excise Tax Act, with provincial harmonization in participating provinces.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 small supplier threshold measured on worldwide taxable supplies from all supplies in the preceding four calendar quarters; a non-resident making taxable supplies in Canada must register once this threshold is exceeded, and suppliers of certain digitally supplied services may be subject to simplified non-resident GST/HST registration requirements.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or government pre-approval mandate exists at the federal level. GST/HST registrants must issue valid invoices containing the supplier's name, BN, description of supply, and tax charged, and must retain electronic records in readable format for at least six years. Pan-Canadian e-invoicing interoperability is optional and not a legal clearance requirement.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods are zero-rated under Part V of Schedule VI to the Excise Tax Act where the supplier delivers the goods outside Canada, retains adequate export evidence, and meets the prescribed conditions; services supplied to non-residents are generally zero-rated where they are not connected to Canadian real property or tangible personal property located in Canada. For MMORPG digital services, zero-rating applies where the service is rendered to a non-resident end-user and the supply is not deemed to be made in Canada.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (CBSA export reporting, including B13A or ACD confirmation)
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill evidencing physical export from Canada
Commercial invoice and packing list reflecting the export sale
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank FX receipt documenting repatriation of export proceeds
Payment-rail evidence from Apple App Store, Google Play, or other platforms where digital export supplies are claimed
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA routinely audits export zero-rating claims; failure to maintain the required export documentation will result in clawback of the 0% rate and reassessment of GST/HST at 5% plus interest from the original remittance date. Normal reassessment periods are four years, but gross negligence or misrepresentation can extend the period and expose the taxpayer to civil penalties of up to 25% of the tax sought, plus additional fines under the Excise Tax Act; wilful evasion may lead to criminal prosecution with fines up to CAD 25,000 and imprisonment. For digital MMORPG revenue, CRA also tests whether supply is deemed made in Canada and whether the platform payout evidence matches the export substantiation bundle.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains a floating exchange rate regime with current account transactions freely convertible at market rates. Capital account transactions require prior notification to the Bank of Canada but are generally convertible subject to reporting and anti-avoidance rules. Profit remittance to non-resident shareholders is permitted after corporate tax payment, subject to beneficial ownership verification, FATCA/CRS compliance, and Income Tax Act provisions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No mandatory surrender of export proceeds is required. Exporters may convert receipts freely upon receipt at prevailing market rates. Voluntary surrender to the Bank of Canada is available solely for statistical purposes without statutory timelines or fixed conversion ratios.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Digital EMIs demonstrate high cross-border viability for low-risk entities but are subject to rigorous AML/KYC obligations, FATCA/CRS reporting, and potential licensing constraints for offshore digital payment processors. Offshore EMIs require enhanced due diligence and may face restrictions on certain transaction types.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote account opening is permitted for standard corporate accounts through video KYC and digital documentation. Physical presence is not mandated for routine onboarding but may be required for accounts exceeding threshold amounts or involving complex ownership structures.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity or unreported foreign control
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Corporate ownership chart, beneficial ownership declarations, shareholder agreements, and proof of tax residency

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source of funds from high-risk jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank references, transaction histories, independent audit reports, and source-of-wealth certifications

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound capital injections via SWIFT MT103 with purpose code 'EQTY' or 'CAPL'. Verification requires source-of-funds documentation, beneficial ownership certificates, and regulatory filings. Wires must reference the recipient's corporate details and purpose for audit trails.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound disbursements utilize SWIFT MT103 for international payments or Commercial Letters of Credit for trade settlements. For MMORPG in-app purchases, direct payouts to Apple App Store and Google Play are permissible via established merchant accounts.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal annual return under the Canada Business Corporations Act
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due within 60 calendar days after the corporation's anniversary date of incorporation, amalgamation, or continuance; not tied to the fiscal year-end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Online filing fee is CAD 12, approximately USD 9; no general statutory late fee applies to online filing. Persistent non-filing may result in compliance notices and administrative dissolution after the statutory default process.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Individuals with Significant Control information filing and annual confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: File with the annual return within 60 calendar days after the anniversary date. File changes to filed information within 15 days after the corporation becomes aware of the change.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to maintain or file required information may constitute an offence under the Canada Business Corporations Act and may expose the corporation and responsible directors or officers to statutory fines; unresolved non-compliance may contribute to dissolution proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due six months after the end of each corporate taxation year. Any balance owing is generally due two months after year-end, or three months for qualifying Canadian-controlled private corporations subject to statutory conditions.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty generally applies where tax is owing, with additional arrears interest and instalment interest potentially accruing. Repeated non-filing may trigger compliance enforcement, reassessment, collection action, and prosecution.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Canada Business Corporations Act, a distributing corporation must appoint an auditor. A non-distributing corporation may dispense with an auditor only by the required unanimous shareholder resolution and subject to applicable corporate-law conditions. Separate lender, shareholder, securities-law, grant, or contractual audit requirements may still apply.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Canadian Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises for eligible private corporations; IFRS is required for publicly accountable enterprises and may be elected where permitted. Tax reporting follows Canadian federal income tax legislation and CRA requirements.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Maintain an accurate register of individuals with significant control and update it promptly following ownership, voting-rights, control, or other relevant changes. Record changes to the ISC register within 15 days after awareness and file the required ISC information with Corporations Canada within the applicable 15-day period; reconfirm and file the current information with each annual return. Update the register of members and securities records for every share issuance or transfer.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members and securities ledger
Register of Directors and prescribed director information
Register of Individuals with Significant Control
Minute book containing director and shareholder resolutions and meeting minutes
Articles, amendments, by-laws, shareholder agreements, and annual filings

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: Approximately USD 250-1,200 annually for a Canadian registered-office and corporate-records service; a registered agent is not a separate federal statutory requirement.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Approximately USD 3,500-15,000 for a private corporation audit, depending on revenue, transaction volume, subsidiaries, shareholder complexity, and reporting framework; an audit is not required where a lawful statutory exemption is used.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holidays exist in Canada. The federal small business deduction reduces the CCPC active business income federal rate to 9% on the first C$500,000 of qualifying active business income, subject to phase-out between C$10M and C$15M taxable capital. Scientific Research and Experimental Development (SR&ED) investment tax credits provide refundable and non-refundable tax relief for qualifying software development. The general federal corporate rate is 15% after the federal abatement and general rate reduction.
